title: Rate of Change Ratio (ROCR)
summary: The ratio of the source now to the source a number of bars back, so 1 is unchanged, above 1 is a rise and below 1 a fall.
description:
Rate of Change Ratio divides the current source value by the value from an earlier bar. A result of 1 means price is where it was, 1.05 means it is 5 percent higher and 0.95 means it is 5 percent lower.

The lookback starts at zero bars and grows by one on each bar whose reference value is present and not zero, until it reaches `length`, then stays there. The line therefore starts on the first bar at exactly 1, and the early readings compare against the first bars of the chart rather than leaving a gap.
howToRead:
Read the line against 1. Above 1, price is higher than it was over the lookback; below 1, it is lower. The distance from 1 is the size of the move as a fraction of the older price, so the reading compares across instruments.

A ratio is lopsided: a fall of 50 percent reads 0.5 while a rise of 50 percent reads 1.5, so large declines look smaller on the chart than large advances of the same percentage. The first `length` bars use a shorter lookback.

settings.label: Source
settings.description: The price series whose ratio to its earlier value is measured. Close is the default.

settings.label: Length
settings.description: The full lookback in bars. The lookback grows to it over the first bars and then stays fixed.

faq.q: Why is the first value exactly 1?
faq.a: The lookback starts at zero bars, so the first bar is divided by itself. The lookback then grows by a bar on each bar until it reaches `length`.

faq.q: How do I turn the ratio into a percentage?
faq.a: Subtract 1 and multiply by 100. A ratio of 1.03 is a rise of 3 percent. The ROCP study plots that percentage directly.
